summary: Fix three silent data bugs that produce wrong output rather than crashing: (1) abc_segment is never included in the by-supplier SQL SELECT so ABC badges always render empty even though the column exists on transactions; (2) the supplier detail Sheet in SupplierPage passes supplier_id to /cube/by-month and /cube/by-category but those endpoints ignore it, so the Sheet always shows engagement-wide totals rather than per-supplier data; (3) the upload UI collects a user-defined column_mapping and passes it to the backend, but _run_pipeline never hands it to ingest_to_raw(), so the mapping is silently discarded and unit_price only populates if the CSV column is literally named unit_price. Also adds backend pytest coverage for the two audit endpoints (GET /batches and GET /batches/{batch_id}) added in the Dashboard Stability Audit sprint.

decisions.abc_segment_aggregation: Use MAX(abc_segment) in the GROUP BY query. After run_cube_pipeline, all transactions for a canonical_supplier_id share the same abc_segment value so MAX is deterministic and correct.
decisions.supplier_id_filter_backwards_compatible: Add supplier_id as an Optional[str] Query param to by-month and by-category endpoints. No existing callers pass it so this is fully backwards-compatible — omitting it returns the current engagement-wide result.
decisions.column_mapping_injection: Add column_mapping: dict | None = None to ingest_to_raw(). If provided and non-empty, inject it as self.mapper.mappings['__ADHOC__'] and call ingest_file(file_path, '__ADHOC__'). The Ingestor is constructed fresh per pipeline run so mutating mappings is safe. The source_row_hash is computed from the raw CSV dict before any mapping, so hashes remain stable regardless of the mapping used.
decisions.audit_test_mock_pattern: For GET /batches/{batch_id} which makes 4 execute() calls in one connection block, use side_effect on mock_conn.execute to return different MagicMock objects for each sequential call.

existing_tables.transactions: Main analytical fact table. Has abc_segment TEXT column (added in analytics foundation sprint, populated by _compute_abc_segments in src/cube/pipeline.py). Also has canonical_supplier_id used for per-supplier filtering.
existing_tables.transactions_raw: Staging table. Has pipeline_status and batch_id columns used by the audit endpoints.
existing_tables.ingestion_batches: Tracks each file upload. Columns: id, engagement_id, filename, row_count, new_rows, duplicate_rows, status, uploaded_at, completed_at.

userStories.title: Add abc_segment to GET /cube/by-supplier response
userStories.description: The get_by_supplier() endpoint in backend/app/routers/cube.py builds a SQL SELECT that includes canonical_supplier_id, canonical_supplier_name, parent_company_name, COUNT(*), SUM(base_amount), AVG(payment_terms_days) — but not abc_segment. The transactions table has an abc_segment TEXT column populated by the cube pipeline via _compute_abc_segments(). After a pipeline run, all transactions rows for a given canonical_supplier_id share the same abc_segment value. Adding MAX(abc_segment) AS abc_segment to the SELECT (compatible with the GROUP BY) will surface it in the API response. The frontend SupplierPage AbcBadge component already references row.abc_segment and renders nothing when it is undefined.

userStories.title: Add supplier_id filter to GET /cube/by-month
userStories.description: The get_by_month() endpoint in backend/app/routers/cube.py at line 263 accepts no query params beyond engagement_id — it has no Optional imports or Query() params. SupplierPage.tsx already passes supplier_id as a query param when fetching per-supplier monthly data for the detail Sheet (line 84-86), but the server ignores it and always returns engagement-wide totals. The fix is to add supplier_id as an optional Query param, then build the SQL WHERE clause dynamically using the same where_clauses list + params dict pattern used in get_by_supplier(). When supplier_id is None, behaviour is identical to today. When set, add AND canonical_supplier_id = :supplier_id.

userStories.title: Wire column_mapping through ingest_to_raw so user column selections are applied
userStories.description: The upload flow collects a user-defined column_mapping dict (e.g. {'Invoice Date': 'invoice_date', 'Supplier Name': 'raw_supplier_name'}) in the RunRequest body. _run_pipeline() in backend/app/routers/ingestion.py already receives column_mapping as a parameter (it is the 4th positional arg, passed from background_tasks.add_task at line 100-102). However, the call to ingestor.ingest_to_raw() at approximately line 283 does not forward it: it passes source_system=None only. Ingestor.ingest_to_raw() in src/ingestion/ingest.py at line 157 needs a new column_mapping: dict | None = None keyword argument. When provided, inject as self.mapper.mappings['__ADHOC__'] = column_mapping and set source_system = '__ADHOC__' so that ingest_file() uses the user-provided mapping. The source_row_hash is computed from raw_row_dicts (the raw CSV before mapping) so hashes are unaffected by this change.
acceptanceCriteria: Edit file: src/ingestion/ingest.py — change the signature of ingest_to_raw() from (self, file_path: str, engine, engagement_id: str, source_system: str = None) to (self, file_path: str, engine, engagement_id: str, source_system: str = None, column_mapping: dict | None = None)

Edit file: src/ingestion/ingest.py — inside ingest_to_raw(), after the line 'batch_id = create_batch(...)' and before the call to 'self.ingest_file(file_path, source_system)', add: if column_mapping: self.mapper.mappings['__ADHOC__'] = column_mapping; source_system = '__ADHOC__'

The column_mapping variable is already in scope as a parameter of _run_pipeline().
